title: The initial conditions for young massive cluster formation in the Galactic Centre: convergence of large-scale gas flows
question: Determine whether star formation is occurring at the scale of individual cores (~1000 au) in Galactic Centre dust ridge cloud ‘d’ (G0.412+0.052) and understand its fate by investigating the gas density distribution and large-scale gas kinematics.

recipe.goal: Image and feather the 1.3 mm dust continuum and image molecular line cubes
recipe.method: Flag line-contaminated channels, image continuum with tclean (automasking), scale Barnes et al. (2019) 259 GHz ALMA+BGPS continuum by 0.6 and combine using CASA feather. Split line windows, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, image with tclean (manual masking), create moment maps with immoments, and smooth spatially with imsmooth.
key_parameters: robust = 0.5, continuum threshold = 15 microJy, 10^5 iterations; line threshold = 0.06 mJy; Gaussian smoothing kernel = 0.34 arcsec
assumptions: Spectral index alpha_nu = 3.75 between 225 GHz and 259 GHz resulting in a flux scaling factor of ~0.6

recipe.goal: Extract compact continuum sources and derive masses, radii, and densities
recipe.method: Compute dendrogram on feathered continuum map using astrodendro to identify leaves, extract integrated flux, and compute masses, effective radii, and spherical volume densities (both with and without background subtraction).
key_parameters: min_value (threshold) = 3 sigma (and 5 sigma for comparison), min_delta (increment) = 1 sigma (sigma = 15 microJy), min_npix = 77
assumptions: Distance d = 8.1 kpc, dust temperature T = 20 K, spectral index beta = 1.75, dust opacity kappa_nu = 0.04 cm^2 g^-1 * (225 GHz / 505 GHz)^1.75, gas-to-dust ratio = 100, spherical geometry

recipe.goal: Search for star formation tracers and outflows towards continuum sources
recipe.method: Inspect 13CO (2-1), CH3CN (12-11), and SiO (5-4) cubes and integrated intensity maps towards the continuum sources, manually inspecting every channel in the SiO cube for outflow morphology.

recipe.goal: Measure nearest neighbour separations and compare with Jeans fragmentation scales
recipe.method: Compute 2D nearest neighbour distances using scikit-learn neighbors, convert to 3D deprojected mean separation lengths by multiplying by ~2.8 (2.3 for PDF expectation value * sqrt(3/2) for 3D deprojection), and compare to thermal and turbulent Jeans lengths and masses of clump 'd6'.
assumptions: Clump 'd6' effective radius = 0.16 pc, mass = 69-239 M_sun, velocity dispersion = 2.1 km/s, gas temperature = 20-40 K

recipe.goal: Perform virial and pressure-bounded hydrostatic equilibrium analysis of sources
recipe.method: Extract leaf-averaged spectra in SiO and three H2CO transitions, fit Gaussian profiles using pyspeckit to measure velocity dispersions from H2CO (3_{0,3}-2_{0,2}), compute virial parameters alpha = 5 R sigma^2 / (G M), aspect ratios, and required confining pressures P_e.
key_parameters: guesses = [max amplitude, velocity at max amplitude, FWHM]; Gamma = 0.73 for pressure-bounded virial equation
assumptions: H2CO (3_{0,3}-2_{0,2}) traces the compact source kinematics; centrally concentrated density structure (Gamma = 0.73)

recipe.goal: Analyze large-scale and small-scale gas kinematics and estimate inflow rates
recipe.method: Construct integrated intensity channel maps (0-30 km/s in 5 km/s bins) of MALT90 HNCO (4_{0,4}-3_{0,3}) and SiO (2-1) and ALMA H2CO (3_{0,3}-2_{0,2}) and SiO (5-4) (5-30 km/s), generate PV diagrams of MALT90 HNCO using CASA impv, and calculate convergence timescales t = d/v and mass inflow rates m_dot = m/t.
key_parameters: Channel map bins = 5 km/s; impv slice widths = 5 pixels (left flow) and 1 pixel (right flow)
assumptions: Velocity along the line of sight is comparable to velocity in the plane of the sky; material sits in the same plane of the sky
